lines.en: She looks pale, and she seems to be worried about something.

lines.en: Maybe she needs a holiday. She seems to work every weekend.

lines.en: Yes, he seems to be upset about the report. It looks wrong to me.
lines.pt: Sim, ele parece chateado com o relatório. Parece errado para mim.

lines.en: The numbers seem to be old. Someone used last year’s file.
lines.pt: Os números parecem ser antigos. Alguém usou o arquivo do ano passado.

lines.en: That sounds like a big mistake. And Anna seems to know about it.
lines.pt: Isso parece um erro grande. E a Anna parece saber disso.

lines.en: Maybe that’s why she looks so stressed.
lines.pt: Talvez seja por isso que ela parece tão estressada.

lines.en: Let’s make her a cup of tea. She seems to like the green one.
lines.pt: Vamos fazer um chá para ela. Parece que ela gosta do verde.

lines.en: Good idea. A cup of tea makes everyone feel better.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Uma xícara de chá faz todo mundo se sentir melhor.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “ela parece cansada” e “ela parece estar preocupada”.
compare.us: Em inglês, use look + adjetivo para o que você vê: she looks pale. Use seem to + verbo para uma impressão geral: she seems to be tired. Depois de look não use to be.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: She seems to be tired.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

facts.label: seem to / look
facts.sub: Use seem to + verbo e look + adjetivo para falar de impressões. Com he e she, o verbo leva s.

facts.label: parece estar
facts.sub: Use seems to be + adjetivo para uma impressão: She seems to be tired. Com she ou he, o verbo leva s: seems.

facts.label: parece (aparência)
facts.sub: Use look + adjetivo para o que você vê: He looks angry. Sem to be e sem advérbio: não use angrily.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: She seems to be tired means it looks like she is tired.
We say “She seems tired to be”.
items.why: We say She seems to be tired.

items.s: Look is followed by an adjective.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: She seems to be tired means it looks like she is tired. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “She seems tired to be”. → Falso (We say She seems to be tired.)
Look is followed by an adjective. → Verdadeiro (Yes: He looks angry.)

pages.title: An office in Glasgow · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning in a Glasgow office. Luisa and Boris sit near the window. The room is quiet and grey. Anna walks in slowly with her bag. Boris watches her sit down. He leans over to talk to Luisa.

“Luisa, Anna seems to be tired today. Is she okay?” says Boris. “She looks pale, and she seems to be worried about something.” says Luisa. “Maybe she needs a holiday. She seems to work every weekend.” says Boris.
